$comment: Camera dropdowns. Each option has a UI label, a prompt fragment written to be concatenated in a fixed order (see PLAN.md 4a), and the numeric parameters the 3D proxy camera must use so the proxy and the prompt describe the same shot. Items marked status=proposed are suggestions awaiting team sign-off.

options.label: Standard · 50mm · f/2.8 · shallow depth of field
options.prompt: Shot with a 50mm lens at f/2.8 for a shallow depth of field, with the main dish and the Coca-Cola bottle in sharp focus and the background falling into soft bokeh.
options.notes: Real depth of field is ~6-9 cm at 1.0-1.2 m, less than the 20-30 cm between entree and bottle, so the prompt names both as the sharp subjects.

options.label: Wide · 35mm · f/1.4 · focus 1.5 m
options.prompt: Shot on a 35mm wide-angle lens (full-frame equivalent) at f/1.4, focused at about 1.5 meters on the main dish and the Coca-Cola bottle, with a shallow depth of field and a softly blurred background.
options.notes: Source said 28-35mm; the proxy needs one value, 35mm chosen for less edge stretch. Source said 'moderate depth of field', but f/1.4 at 1.5 m gives ~15 cm (35mm) to ~24 cm (28mm), which is shallow, so the wording was corrected. Focus distance fixes camera-to-MAIN distance at ~1.5 m, so this is a wider, more environmental frame.

options.label: Ultra-wide · 15mm rectilinear · street food
options.prompt: Shot on an ultra-wide 15mm rectilinear lens at f/8 with deep depth of field, the food and the Coca-Cola bottle sharp, straight verticals and no fisheye distortion.
options.notes: Source said 14-16mm; 15mm used for the proxy. No aperture was given; f/8 proposed. 'Photorealistic street food photography' moved out of the lens text into the scene/genre text so it only appears for street scenes. Ultra-wides stretch objects near the frame edges, so the SKU is kept out of the outer 15% to protect the logo.

options.label: Low · 10°
options.prompt: Low camera angle, about 10 degrees above the tabletop, close to the diner's eye level.
options.notes: At low angles items hide behind each other more, so fewer items fit without breaking the no-stacking rule. The solver reports infeasible rather than stacking.

options.label: Medium · 25°
options.prompt: Camera angled about 25 degrees down toward the table.

options.label: Diner's eye · 30° (brand default)
options.prompt: Diner's-eye view, camera angled about 30 degrees down toward the table.
options.notes: The composition rules set ~30° as the default; it was missing from the list.

options.label: High · 45°
options.prompt: Camera angled about 45 degrees down toward the table.
options.notes: Upper end of the 30-45° range allowed by the blueprint schema. Overhead (90°) stays excluded by the composition rules.
